userStories.title: Build the pure PRD-oracle linter module (named-rules scanner + PRD walk)
userStories.description: As the plan phase, I need a pure, exported linter that scans a PRD's acceptanceCriteria oracle shell strings for the self-nullifying grep -q + -L/-l absence idiom, so a semantically-broken oracle is caught deterministically without the LLM auditor.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure exported scanner is structured as a named-rules list (array of { name, test(command): finding | null }) with the grep-q-plus-list-files rule as the sole current member, so adding a future rule is a one-liner. [oracle: grep -qE 'name.*test' src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts]

The grep rule flags any grep invocation whose flags include the quiet flag -q AND a list-files flag -L or -l in ANY order, spacing, or bundling: it must flag -Lq, -qL, -lq, -ql, -L -q, -l -q, and a bundled/reordered form; it matches the general class, never the literal substring '-Lq'. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts]

The correct absence idiom '! grep -q PATTERN file' does NOT trigger the rule; a plain 'grep -q' match assertion, 'grep -L' alone, 'grep -l' alone, and non-grep commands all pass. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts]

The linter walks each userStory's acceptanceCriteria[], reusing parseOracleDirectives (src/supervisor/behavioral-gate.ts) to extract the [oracle: ...] .command shell string for named-command and file-assert directives, and applies the rules; criteria with no oracle, reviewer-judgment, or tmux-pty directives are skipped. [oracle: grep -q 'parseOracleDirectives' src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts]

Each finding carries the story id, the offending oracle command string, the rule name, and a why-broken description, and the walk consumes the minimal PrdShape/PrdStory read-model shape (src/commands/status.ts). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts]

Unit tests hit real oracle strings with no I/O and cover: the six flagged grep forms, the four passing grep/non-grep cases, and that a criterion without an [oracle:] suffix yields no finding. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New module src/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.ts + test/supervisor/prd-oracle-lint.test.ts. This is the FIRST structured PRD content validator (no prd.schema.json exists; prd.json is parsed ad-hoc at ~6 sites). Reuse parseOracleDirectives/parseOracleDirective (behavioral-gate.ts:137-169) to turn a criterion string into an OracleDirective and consume .command; do NOT re-implement oracle parsing. No full shell tokenizer needed: greenfield regex/flag-class matching modeled on scripts/check-test-sleeps.ts pure-scanner shape. Detection MUST be the general class (grep -q co-occurring with -L or -l in any arrangement), never the literal '-Lq' substring (mirrors CAM-0309.json:21). Reuse the PrdShape/PrdStory read-model (src/commands/status.ts:165-179) for the walk; noUncheckedIndexedAccess means array/regex-group access is T|undefined, always guard. Em-dash literal-escape oracle class is OUT OF SCOPE. Grep patterns.md for 'oracle' before coding.

userStories.title: Wire the linter into the plan-runner audit path, folding findings into the re-plan loop
userStories.description: As the plan phase, I need the deterministic oracle linter to run in runPlanWorkerSequence after the prd.json presence guard and before the auditor spawns, so a broken oracle becomes a deterministic BLOCK that re-plans without spending the auditor and fails closed before branch creation.
acceptanceCriteria: runPlanWorkerSequence gains an injected content-reading seam that reads and parses the prd.json content in-process (a new seam distinct from readPlannerReportFn, which stays presence-only, plan-runner.ts:318-322), kept in the module's existing dependency-injection style rather than a raw inline fs read. [oracle: grep -qE 'Prd|prdContent|readPrd' src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts]

The linter runs AFTER the isPlannerNoPrd presence guard (~:792) and BEFORE resolveAndSpawnAuditor (~:798); when it finds a broken oracle the auditor subagent is never spawned for that round. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts]

A lint finding is folded into the EXISTING audit-BLOCK machinery: runPlanWorkerSequence returns a synthetic { kind: 'audit-blocked', issue, report } whose report is a well-formed PlanVerdictReport (verdict 'BLOCK', summary, findings[] carrying story id + offending oracle string + rule name + why-broken as PlanVerdictFinding), so the runPlanPhaseWithReplan loop re-plans the same issue via buildReplanPlannerTaskPrompt with the lint findings as feedback. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts]

Exhausting the re-plan rounds on a persistently-broken oracle writes the same escalation marker the auditor-BLOCK exhaustion path writes (writeEscalationMarkerFn / plan-escalated terminal), never proceeding to branch creation. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts]

Flow ordering is verified end-to-end (plan -> lint -> lint-fail => re-plan without spending the auditor -> auditor -> audit-block => re-plan): a planner-produced prd.json with a broken grep -q + -L oracle triggers the re-plan loop before the auditor is spawned, while a clean prd.json (all oracles well-formed) proceeds to the auditor unchanged with zero behavior change. [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Touches src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts + test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts. PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING: this is NOT a check:all gate (prd.json is ephemeral, in-process only during plan phase, committed at plan-runner.ts:1178, git rm'd at ship). Fail closed: do NOT auto-repair the oracle string; route it to the planner via re-plan feedback. Consume the synthetic-BLOCK path so the existing runPlanPhaseWithReplan while-loop (plan-runner.ts:956) and its writeEscalationMarkerFn seam handle re-plan + escalation with zero new terminal. PlanVerdictReport/PlanVerdictFinding shape lives in src/supervisor/plan-verdict-report.ts ({ verdict, summary, findings:[{ id, category, severity, storyId?, description, suggestion? }] }). buildReplanPlannerTaskPrompt(issueId, findings) already embeds priorFindings. Independent of CAM-309 (no blockedBy): keep the broken-class definition consistent but do NOT assume 309's agent-prose changes are present. Depends on US-001's exported linter. Grep patterns.md for 'plan-runner' / 're-plan' before coding.
